analysis.title: Harness growth, manage risks: Building portfolio resilience
key_insights: UBS CIO sees a constructive 2027 with robust growth and solid earnings prospects, but says risks from geopolitics, inflation, government debt sustainability and AI monetization are increasing.
UBS downgrades global equities to Neutral. Investors with equity exposure above their longer-term strategic allocation should consider rebalancing toward it.

AI infrastructure investment was the most important growth driver this year. UBS expects the spending to keep rising in 2027 but more slowly, which should still support growth and private consumption while tempering market euphoria.
UBS expects corporate earnings growth of about 15% in the US and Eurozone and about 20% in Asia ex-Japan by the end of 2027, and double-digit returns in all major markets.
UBS strategists see the SMI at 15,500 at end-2027 and do not expect the Swiss market to keep pace with foreign equity markets.

Investors should check how dependent their portfolios are on a few companies, such as AI beneficiaries. UBS says earnings growth should be more evenly spread across sectors in 2027, which makes a focus on large technology companies less compelling.
Swiss investors should review domestic concentration. Certain pharmaceutical stocks gained significantly from the rotation into defensives, which could dampen their 2027 performance outlook.

Income sources: Swiss rates are low and currency hedging costs are high, so UBS sees limited opportunity for positive real returns from high-quality bonds. It sees opportunities in high yield and emerging market bonds, with greater credit and currency risk.
Other income sources UBS names are dividend-paying stocks, hedge funds and infrastructure, and options or structured return strategies.

Investors should test whether portfolios would hold up if weaker growth, higher inflation or lower returns on AI investment materialized, using diversification across asset classes, regions, sectors and style factors.
Investors holding too few equities can build positions gradually toward their long-term target. Those holding too many should consider a more defensive stance.

sector_views.rationale: UBS says a primary focus on large technology companies is less compelling because earnings growth should broaden across sectors in 2027.
Certain pharma stocks gained significantly from the rotation into defensives, which could dampen their 2027 performance outlook.

earnings_insights: UBS forecasts corporate earnings growth of about 15% in the US and Eurozone and about 20% in Asia ex-Japan by the end of 2027 (UBS forecast).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Low Swiss rates and high currency hedging costs leave limited opportunity for positive real returns from high-quality bonds.

risk_factors: Whether AI investment delivers the hoped-for returns.
Weaker growth or higher inflation than assumed.
Credit and currency risk in high yield and emerging market bonds.
Concentration in a small number of companies, including certain Swiss pharmaceutical stocks.
vol_and_positioning: UBS refers to a period of higher volatility and says options or structured return strategies are one source of income.
Concentration risk: portfolios heavily exposed to a few AI beneficiaries are less resilient.
geopolitical: The report lists geopolitics among risks likely to come into sharper market focus in the coming months, and says the global economy weathered geopolitical crises and another energy shock this year.

tension_points.bull_case: Robust growth, solid earnings prospects (about 15% growth in the US and Eurozone, about 20% in Asia ex-Japan) and double-digit expected returns in all major markets, with AI spending still rising.
tension_points.bear_case: Rising risks from geopolitics, inflation, government debt sustainability and AI monetization, and slower AI spending growth that may temper market euphoria.

theme_stances.key_argument: Risks are increasing and the balance between opportunities and risks is more even than in 2026, though earnings prospects still support a Neutral allocation.
theme_stances.evidence: we have downgraded our view on equities to Neutral

theme_stances.key_argument: Excessive concentration in a few AI beneficiaries can weaken portfolio resilience, and earnings growth should broaden across sectors in 2027.
theme_stances.evidence: Excessive concentration, such as exposure focused on a few AI beneficiaries
